Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rJavaEnv 0.4.0

Breaking and behaviour changes

  • Installed Java environments and project links now use the layout <platform>/<arch>/<distribution>/<backend>/<version>, so different vendors and backends of the same version can coexist. Environments in the 0.3.0 layout (<platform>/<arch>/<version>) are still listed, and existing project .Rprofile settings keep pointing to them.
  • Downloaded archive names now include their backend, preventing native and SDKMAN downloads from reusing each other’s files. Older archives are left in place and are not reused (#107).
  • Setup now protects rJava’s JVM selection. With the released rJava, a loaded but uninitialized rJava namespace is treated as unverified: java_ensure() errors before changing environment variables, because the namespace may already have locked its JVM library path. Restart R before setup in that case (see rJava issues #334 and #25).
  • Compatibility probes no longer load rJava or start its JVM in the calling process: java_check_version_rjava() runs in a separate R process, and command-version checks execute the selected JDK without preloading libjvm and restore temporary environment variables on every exit.
  • Dependencies: jsonlite was replaced by RcppSimdJson, and digest, memoise, rlang, withr and yaml were added to Imports. callr is a new suggested package, needed by with_rjava_env().

New features

Ensure and resolve Java

  • New java_ensure() checks the active session, then system installations, then rJavaEnv’s cache, and downloads only when nothing suitable is found. It does nothing when a valid Java is already active. check_against = "rJava" (default) refuses to select Java that rJava could no longer use; check_against = "cmd" configures command-line Java only (#92).
  • New java_resolve() finds or installs a Java and returns its JAVA_HOME without changing environment variables.
  • New scoped helpers: local_java_env() and with_java_env() set JAVA_HOME and PATH for command-line Java and restore them on exit; with_rjava_env() runs a function in a fresh R process with the requested Java for rJava (#92).
  • New java_check_compatibility() reports whether an already running rJava JVM meets a version requirement, without loading rJava or calling .jinit().
  • New java_find_system() lists Java installations from JAVA_HOME, PATH, versioned JAVA_HOME_<major> variables (including CI architecture suffixes) and platform-specific locations.
  • New java_get_home(), a shortcut for Sys.getenv("JAVA_HOME") (#85).
  • java_quick_install() now invisibly returns the path to JAVA_HOME.

Version requirements

  • version accepts a major version (21), a specific numeric version ("21.0.9", "11.0.29", or legacy spellings such as "1.8.0_452"), or an SDKMAN identifier ("25.0.1-amzn"), which selects the SDKMAN backend.
  • type = "exact" or type = "min" selects exact or minimum matching in java_ensure(), java_resolve(), local_java_env() and with_java_env().
  • Specific (patch-level) requirements are strict in java_resolve() and the functions built on it (java_ensure(), local_java_env(), with_java_env() and with_rjava_env()): system, active and cached candidates are compared by their full runtime version, candidates are ordered numerically, and a fresh download is verified after unpacking. If a vendor API returned a different release than requested, java_ensure() returns FALSE and the others error. java_quick_install(), use_java(), java_download() and java_install() do not check the installed runtime, and the native Zulu backend may return another release of the requested major version.
  • accept_system_java = FALSE ignores system and active JDKs and uses only managed installations, filtered by distribution, backend, platform and architecture.
  • java_valid_versions() falls back to a dynamic range of major versions when vendor APIs are unreachable, so new Java releases do not require a package update.

Distributions and download backends

  • Eclipse Temurin and Azul Zulu are supported in addition to Amazon Corretto.
  • New backend argument ("native" or "sdkman"), also settable with options(rJavaEnv.backend = ...). The native backend uses vendor APIs and verifies SHA-256 checksums. The SDKMAN backend covers more builds but cannot verify checksums and warns about it (#98).
  • New java_list_available() lists installable versions from the native backend, SDKMAN, or both, for the current or a given platform and architecture.
  • java_unpack() and java_install() gain distribution, backend and force arguments (#86).
  • The cache management functions java_list_project(), java_list_installed(), java_list_distrib(), java_clear_project(), java_clear_installed() and java_clear_distrib() are now exported.

Linux and building rJava from source

  • On Linux, libjvm.so is located and loaded with dyn.load() when Java is set, so rJava and dependent packages load with the selected Java. Command-only setup (check_against = "cmd") does not preload it.
  • New java_build_env_set() and java_build_env_unset() set, in the session or the project .Rprofile, the variables needed to install rJava from source on macOS, Linux and Windows without R CMD javareconf. System requirements still apply; see the new vignette “Install ‘rJava’ from source”.

rJava: released behaviour and experimental deferred loading

  • With released rJava, configure Java before loading the rJava namespace. Once rJava has loaded, restart R before selecting another JVM, or use with_rjava_env() for a separate process. All documented patterns rely only on released rJava.
  • Experimental, optional: rJava builds with deferred JVM loading (explored in rJava’s feature/dynamic branch) expose a JVM state API. When that state confirms that no JVM library is loaded, no JVM is initialized, and no native host has already mapped a JVM, java_ensure() permits setup after the namespace has loaded and skips the Linux libjvm preload. If the state is missing, unknown or reports a loaded JVM, the released-rJava behaviour applies. rJavaEnv does not require these builds.

Performance

  • Version checks and system scans can be memoised within the session with .use_cache = TRUE in java_check_version_cmd(), java_check_version_rjava(), java_find_system(), java_ensure(), java_resolve() and local_java_env(). Caching is opt-in; the default .use_cache = FALSE always performs a fresh check. Version-check caches are keyed by the effective JAVA_HOME.

Bug fixes and minor improvements

  • More robust Java home and version detection: symlinks are resolved, ANSI output is cleaned, versions without a minor component are parsed, and Rscript is located more reliably (#82, #95).
  • macOS no longer picks up the /usr/bin/java stubs as a Java installation (#96).
  • java_check_version_rjava() works on Linux after installing Java (#100, #101).
  • Live Java checks are isolated in subprocesses, and Temurin version discovery uses release assets (#103).
  • Zulu requests for a specific version no longer combine the version filter with latest=true in the API query.
  • SDKMAN support adapts to upstream API schema changes and fixes path resolution (#104). Broker resolution handles rejected catalogue identifiers, reads redirect URLs without downloading the archive into memory, and retries transient API failures (#105).
  • Plain SDKMAN major- and patch-version requests exclude JavaFX, CRaC, early-access and snapshot builds unless requested explicitly. Fresh SDKMAN downloads report the resolved identifier and respect quiet = TRUE; cached archives are reused without resolving an identifier (#107). SDKMAN catalogues can lag vendor releases; use backend = "native" when an entry is stale or unavailable (#106).
  • Download progress in java_download() respects quiet.
  • java_check_version_cmd() and java_check_version_rjava() document that they return FALSE when Java cannot be found or checked.
  • rlang is declared as a dependency, so functions work right after installation.

Documentation and testing

  • New developer vignette on integrating rJavaEnv into packages: passive probes, explicit setup, eager and lazy rJava dependencies, and subprocess isolation.
  • Minimal downstream consumer packages exercise these contracts in fresh R processes on Linux, macOS and Windows in continuous integration.
  • Live download tests, SDKMAN contract tests and a daily SDKMAN API canary run on a schedule.

rJavaEnv 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2025-04-04

New features

  • Java version (currently still only for Amazon Corretto) is now determined dynamically using the official GitHub json with releases, so when new Java version becomes available, you will not be depenent on rJavaEnv to be updated. As a fallback, versions up to 24 are hardcoded.

  • Added force argument to java_download(). When set to TRUE, allows to overwrite the distribution file if it already exist in the cache. This save the trouble of deleting the cached file with java_clear() before re-downloading.

  • Added a new function java_valid_versions() allows to retrieve a list of all available Java versions for the current automatically detected OS and CPU architecture, or user-specified platform and architecture.

Improvements

  • Better command line Java detection (thanks to Jonas Lieth)

  • Test coverage is now 7.2%

rJavaEnv 0.2.2 (2024-09-13)

CRAN release: 2024-09-13

  • Hot fix: improve robustness of setting Java environment in the current session with either use_java() or java_quick_install(). See bug fix below.

  • Bug fix: Setting Java environment via rJava::.jniInitialized() rendered impossible changing Java version for rJava-dependent packages, because it somehow pre-initialised rJava

rJavaEnv 0.2.1 (2024-09-03)

CRAN release: 2024-09-03

  • Documentation and description clean-up

rJavaEnv 0.2.0 (2024-08-28)

  • Breaking change: java_check_version_cmd() and java_check_version_rjava() now return detected Java version instead of TRUE/FALSE

  • New function use_java() to download, install and set Java from cache for the current sesssion, without touching the current project/working directory. This is intended for use with targets and callr.

  • New vignette on using the package with targets' and 'callr

  • Updated documentation with clearer instructions on cache folder cleanup before removing the package

  • Depends on R > 4.0 to be able to write to the package cache directory without extra user warning. Cache cleanup and management functions are provided, as well as the documentation in both README and vignettes.

rJavaEnv 0.1.2

CRAN release: 2024-08-26

  • Fixed broken links in README.md

rJavaEnv 0.1.1

  • Improved documentation

  • Better handling of cache directory

  • Bug fixes and changes to address CRAN reviewer’s comments to the first submission

rJavaEnv 0.1.0
